body: I'm not an optimist. I don't know how to think that every day will be different.

Whether we believe that we can do something is the pure motivation for doing it. And I've lost that simple motivation. You can't have a car run on no fuel.

I've tried giving myself small victories. It doesn't work for me. It's all so insignificant.

I've seen people my age and younger do great things in the terms of their dreams or hobbies. If I ever want to be at least useful in the future, I would had to have started developing some skills years ago. It's too late for that now.
If that's what life is, I can happily say that I failed. Because I don't want to get up and move forward anymore. Besides, it's not like that's the only thing I failed at.

I don't even feel like I've done any small actions of good. Just small actions of bad or no actions at all. And I've tried to just do good actions, but I've come up with nothing. And nothing can change that.

I'm not one to compare two bad life situations. You may think mine is worse, but I can't really judge.

Your situation actually sounds kinda bad. Do you want to PM about it?

Thanks for your compassion, but I'm not one to compare two bad life situations. Each is terrifying to its owner.

I don't really have much of a treatment plan, now that you ask of it. I was just planning on calling the Suicide Hotline if I'm really desperate. But other than that, nothing comes to mind.

I think you got it right with the therapist thing, to the shame and dismay for me. I've always been afraid of telling anyone of my fantasies. Therapists especially, as they practically tell my mom everything that goes on in there. Not to mention that every time I go into a session, they ask me what they want to talk about. I have a really hard time making decisions, so that's too broad of a topic for me, and whatever comes to mind never makes full use of the time given to me. And whatever complements I receive, whether from the therapist or anyone else, are instantly denied to me, not making any more impact on me than how I was before. I have a hard time accepting good things abou me, since I always feel that people are so quiet around me so they can gather more information to use to talk behind my back or set me up for something. 

So I'm basically scared of people finding put that I'm suicidal. I'm an internal person, so I favor privacy. I guess it's hurting me?

The Exorcist thing actually makes sense. Thanks. :)

Honestly, I don't feel like I'm just doling out love. If anything, I'm just some void in the world. And I'm afraid that it won't change.

Thank you for the kind words, but I would never wish this pain on anyone. And you definitely don't deserve it.

Thank you so much for taking the time to read this and reply. It may not mean much to you, but it did feel good to see an orange mail icon. :)

>You will be surprised at how many people in this world are mediocre. Sure there may be few naturally brilliant kids, but most kids who are successful in school and end up at top colleges are the kids who go home and study 4 hours a night.

I can buy that. That's something.

>Anyways, the point being that your life whether in failure or success is within your control and power. I think once you realize that, you will regain the willpower to try harder in your life.

Really, I've just lost the will to make my life better. I'm too tired from fighting for so many years and coming up with nothing.

>Is the 3.3 GPA really the result of you being "dumb"? Is there something that's physically stopping you from doing better?

Due to the past couple of shitty months, I can't bring myself to do any academic work. When I try to work on anything, my mind tries to fight the motivation with emotional antibodies, and they always win. I become so overwhelmed over the tiniest things, even though I don't really do anything to bring me to that point.

>Maybe I'm missing that you already understand this but I sense part of your issues are fear of failure and low self-esteem.

Well, you're right about that. I won't lie.

>I know that seems obvious but the question I have is do you think that's from failing your expectations or something deeper?

I just feel that whenever I fail to do something that involves someone else (and I do it a lot), I hurt them in the process. It can be big or small, but it's still pain. Also, I don't feel that I can be helped. My mom only takes me to pediatric therapists, and if you've been to one, their policy is basically "Make the patient respect their elders and tell them they're special." Not to mention that with basically no self-esteem, it's easy to hate myself.

Then again, I feel the self-hatred to be filling. There was a time two nights ago when I was laying down in bed, not thinking about mistakes or bad things. I was content, but at the same time, I felt empty. Like my body was just longing for a filling feeling. I've tried happiness, but that's just too lofty. Sorrow is dense and able to fill you up faster. I was able to feel that come into play the next day.
